title: No phonograph at home, the theaters as his school
summary: Without records at home, the stage shows were his main source of music, more than the movies.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: But, I -- you know -- as I say my grandaunt had this Victrola. And, I used to go over there and do some things and chores for her over there, you know what I mean.
Yeah.
So I can get in that room. (laugh)

Yeah. Well, listen Freddie -- when you got up to New York -- weren't you guys -- didn't any of you guys start to try to buy a couple of records? Did anybody have a phonograph? At home? Up in New York? Or were there -- there weren't jukeboxes sold?
No, no, no. I don't remember that -- I don't think anybody in my family -- I don't think we had any --
No.
No.
Well, listen -- so, your experience really was in getting into those theaters?
Yeah. Yeah.
That was really the --
It was a part of me, more or less. You know what I mean?
That was it. you always did.
I really liked the theater.
Yeah.
See?
Yeah. Right.
That was then more than the moving pictures.
Oh, yeah.

Yeah. The movies -- well, I used to go to the movies and see the series (serials) and what not, you know, they used to have down south, more or less. You know, those -- next week -- those chapter things.
Yeah. Yeah.
I used to go over there --
Yeah.
But, the minute a -- you know -- a stage show would come to town I would -- you know -- I would --
Yeah. Yeah.
So now -- -- Go down there and --
I don't know why, you know? Looking back on it now.
That was your thing
But, that's -- I would spend most of my time in the theaters, more or less.
